newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs urge peaceful solution to Albania crisis.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs urge peaceful solution to Albania crisis.

text.p: The European Parliament called on Thursday on the rebel groups holding the south of Albania to lay down their arms and urged President Sali Barisha to stick by his promise to grant them an amnesty.
The parliament backed the compromise hammered out between Barisha and the 10 opposition parties on March 9, insisting that all sides should seek a "peaceful and democratic" solution to the crisis.
The compromise provides for a general amnesty, the surrender of weapons and the creation of a government of national unity to lead the country to elections by June.
Parliament's resolution asked the European Union to appoint a special envoy to south east Europe to help prevent crises such as that being witnessed in Albania.
It also urged the EU and international financial institutions to help Albania out of its economic quagmire, on condition that Tirana committed itself to improving democracy and ungagging the media.
The assembly said the EU should help with investigations into the failed pyramid investment schemes, whose collapse sparked off the crisis.

Dutch European Affairs Minister Michel Patijn told parliament on Wednesday the collapse of the schemes had defrauded small investors of savings worth 40 to 60 percent of the country's gross domestic product.

Hans van den Broek, the European Commissioner in charge of relations with central and eastern Europe, on Wednesday appealed to the political forces in Albania to stick strictly to the terms of a potential compromise, warning that the country could collapse if they did not.
"One thing is clear, if the compromise doesn't stand, doesn't hold up, then things will get much worse in Albania and there will be an uncontrolled rebellion," he said.
